notes: NEGATIVE RESULT: no known public memory-safety bug in RBU (ext/rbu/sqlite3rbu.c, Resumable Bulk Update). WHERE I LOOKED: (1) the complete NVD dump of all 264 CVEs mentioning 'sqlite', published 2006-01 through 2026-08-31, regex 'rbu' -- ZERO hits; (2) the NVD CPE set for cpe:sqlite:sqlite (67 records, strict subset) -- zero; (3) full text of sqlite.org/cves.html (updated 2026-08-01) -- no occurrence of 'RBU'; (4) a targeted web search for 'sqlite3rbu.c crash buffer overflow' returned only session-extension and FTS5 results, no RBU hit. POSITIVE CONTROL: the identical method returns CVE-2023-7104, CVE-2026-50812 and CVE-2026-50813 for the SIBLING extension (session), which lives under the same 'needs a compile flag, parses adversary binary' description -- so the zero is not the query failing. INTERPRETATION: RBU is far less deployed and, unlike session, is not wired into an in-tree fuzz harness (sessionfuzz exists; there is no rbufuzz equivalent in the published test set) -- absence of found bugs here most likely reflects absence of LOOKING. Needs -DSQLITE_ENABLE_RBU. Not in a default build and NOT in our Capstone build: capstone/benchmarks/sqlite/build-sqlite-capstone.sh passes no -DSQLITE_ENABLE_* for it. CLAIM MADE AND REJECTED ON VERIFICATION (this survey, 2026-09-02): a research pass asserted this negative was wrong. I tried to confirm it and could not, so THE NEGATIVE STANDS and the claim is recorded here rather than acted on. The claim was that RBU 'has a heap buffer overflow with a working public ASAN PoC'. It arrived with NO check-in hash, NO forum URL and NO CVE. My own targeted search for an RBU/sqlite3rbu.c heap overflow returned only session, FTS5, zipfile and shell results -- nothing on RBU. Unfalsifiable as stated, so not entered. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES THIS WORTH RECORDING: two other negatives in this survey (geopoly, pager/WAL) WERE correctly overturned, and in both cases the evidence was specific and independently checkable -- real check-in hashes I fetched and confirmed. This one was not. The lesson is that the negatives here fall to evidence, not to expectation. METHOD NOTE, corroborated independently by two separate investigations: OSS-FUZZ IS STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO ALL OF ext/. test/ossfuzz.c includes only sqlite3.h and registers no extension, and projects/sqlite3/build.sh is a plain `../configure --shared=0`, so none of ext/misc/*, ext/expert/*, ext/session/* or ext/rbu/* is linked into the fuzz target. Consistent with the separate finding that 'ossfuzz' matches 94 SQLite check-ins while 'ossfuzz rtree' and 'ossfuzz geopoly' each match 0. So 'no OSS-Fuzz issue' is worth NOTHING as evidence for any extension in this file; only SQLite's in-house dbsqlfuzz reaches these files.
